First, create a restricted user account and use that. Only use the admin account for specific tasks. Set the admin wallpaper yellow or something so you don't forget where you are, disable UAC. If you want to get even fancier, have your common readonly applications (pdf reader, media player, etc) launch as "guest" and set the appropriate folders as readable by guest.

Fix your hosts file with this:

https://someonewhocares.org/hosts/

Configure your name server, I'd been using 1.1.1.1 and it's fine. (I've since switched to HNS, if this option works for you, give it a go)

Remove all the applications you don't use, kill any services you dont use.

Move your user profile to a separate drive, real or virtual and encrypt profile (to you) as well as all drives (to the OS).

Download TOR browser for anything questionable and only for questionable things. Using a secured environment all the time leads to leaks. Use a normal environment for all basic use, change browsers (I mean, a VM would be better, but more complex) to perform specific, riskier activities.

To follow up on my other comment, I see a lot of specific product recommendations... Linux over Windows, Brave over Chrome, etc.

Most consumer level products are security/privacy equivalent under normal situations. Pick software with features you like and are familiar with. (e.g. TOR browser isn't more secure, it just has access to TOR as an easy to use feature.)

Also, feel free to ask if you don't understand why/how of any of my suggestions. The internet is a battlefield, and herd immunity works.
